name: MathVista
description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (i.e., IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). Completing these tasks requires fine-grained, deep visual understanding and compositional reasoning.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research)
citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024.
rai:dataCollection: MathVista was collected through three main approaches: (1) Collection of 9 existing MathQA datasets in multimodal settings, including datasets for geometry problem solving, math word problems with visual contexts, and textbook question answering on college curricula, limited to 400 examples per source dataset for balanced representation (2,666 examples total). (2) Review and collection of 19 existing VQA datasets containing math-related instances. Examples were initially selected using heuristic rules (numeric answers or quantity words in questions), yielding 4,949 candidates. Three expert annotators then manually labeled these to determine mathematical reasoning involvement using majority voting, resulting in 2,739 examples (limited to 400 per source). (3) Creation of three new datasets: IQTest (228 examples requiring inductive reasoning on puzzle test figures), FunctionQA (400 examples on algebraic reasoning with functional plots), and PaperQA (107 examples on scientific reasoning with academic figures from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface). All new dataset questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through rigorous review with 99.2% inter-annotation consistency.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets), puzzle test figures from online learning platforms (for IQTest), functional plots (for FunctionQA), and academic papers with informative illustrations released in August 2023 on Huggingface (for PaperQA).
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: August 2023 (for PaperQA dataset collection from Huggingface papers)
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, automatic filtration was performed using heuristic rules to select examples likely involving mathematical reasoning (examples with numeric answers or quantity words in questions). This yielded 4,949 candidates. Subsequently, three expert annotators manually labeled these examples to determine mathematical reasoning involvement, with majority voting applied. Each source dataset was limited to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. Quality checks were conducted to address unidentified errors. The dataset was divided into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples) subsets using a sampling strategy to maintain distribution similarity (KL Divergence: 0.008, TV distance: 0.035).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For the three newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA), all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields. A two-step review process ensured consistency: (1) Each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, achieving 99.2% inter-annotation consistency rate (only 6 disagreements among 736 questions). (2) Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team to reach consensus. For VQA dataset selection, three expert annotators labeled examples to determine mathematical reasoning involvement using majority voting. Metadata annotations (question type, answer type, task category, grade level, visual context, mathematical reasoning skills) were obtained from source dataset details, with automatic annotation verified by manual labeling of 1,000 examples showing 94.1% exact match and 98.79% individual label accuracy.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom GUI annotation tool (illustrated in Figure 23 for new datasets and Figure 24 for mathematical reasoning labeling)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For metadata annotation verification, expert annotators manually labeled mathematical reasoning categories for 1,000 examples. Results showed 94.1% of examples had exact same set of reasoning types between automatic and human annotations, while 98.79% of individual labels were identical, indicating high accuracy of automatic annotation. Inter-annotation agreement analysis using Fleiss Kappa score yielded 0.775, indicating substantial consistency among annotators.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (for quality verification during new dataset creation and VQA dataset selection)
rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields (for new dataset annotation). For human performance baseline: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with satisfactory annotation history, successful qualification test completion, and high school degree or higher.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains 6.57% non-English questions including Chinese and Persian. Grade level metadata includes elementary school, high school, and college levels. Some images contain people (e.g., celebrities for age gap questions), though one model (Multimodal Bard) restricted responses to images of people.
rai:dataBiases: The authors note that questions in IQTest are biased toward puzzle test figures from online learning platforms. The dataset focuses on mathematical reasoning in visual contexts spanning specific domains like science and college-level math, which may limit generalizability to other domains. The paper acknowledges that while the dataset encompasses multiple visual contexts and mathematical reasoning abilities, certain scenarios may remain unaddressed. The dataset contains only 6.57% non-English questions, indicating potential language bias toward English.
rai:dataLimitations: The authors acknowledge several limitations: (1) Dataset coverage gaps - while encompassing broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, certain types of mathematical problems and visuals may not be represented. (2) Scalability concerns - the focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts spanning specific domains (science, college-level math) necessitates more labor-intensive data collection compared to textual-only or general-purpose datasets, limiting scalability and generalizability to other domains. (3) Annotation heterogeneity - only 85.6% of examples have annotations sourced from original providers, and these lack unified format/structure (e.g., logic forms from Geometry3K, natural language solutions from TabMWP, theorems from TheoremQA). (4) The study focused exclusively on most recent and prominent models available at time of research. (5) Potential data noise requiring refinement based on community feedback.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts. It can be used for: (1) Testing and benchmarking large language models (LLMs) and large multimodal models (LMMs) on mathematical reasoning tasks, (2) Model development validation using the testmini subset (1,000 examples), (3) Standard evaluation using the test subset (5,141 examples). The test set answer labels are not publicly released to prevent data contamination, with an online evaluation platform maintained. The benchmark is intended to facilitate development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks.
